channel.title: The Local Europe - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Local Europe (thelocal.com)

item.title: Is Paris really going to ban second homes?
item.description: The city of Paris has been introducing more stringent measures against second homes, in an attempt to ease the capital's housing shortage, but will it really go as far as banning them altogether?

item.title: EU says countries can halt EES checks over summer to avoid travel chaos
item.description: Member States will have the green light to partially suspend Europe's Entry/Exit System (EES), the new EU digital border system, over the summer to avoid any travel chaos at ports and airports during peak season.

item.title: OPINION: TV anchor's child sex conviction reveals hypocrisy of French right-wingers
item.description: Hypocrisy knows no political boundaries - writes John Lichfield - it can occur on the Left, on the Right and in the Centre. France is currently witnessing a particularly extreme and puzzling case of hypocrisy on the moralising, hard Right.

item.title: What jurisdiction do French courts have over people outside France?
item.description: It's not uncommon for French prosecutors to launch investigations into people or businesses - but what jurisdiction do French courts have over those outside France?

item.title: X slams 'politicised' France after French prosecutors summon Musk
item.description: French prosecutors on Tuesday searched the Paris offices of Elon Musk's X as part of an investigation into alleged political interference and sexual deepfakes and summoned Musk in what the social media giant slammed as "politicised" raids.

item.title: How Brits who arrived in Germany before Brexit can get permanent residency
item.description: British people who were living in Germany by the end of 2020 have their residence rights protected under the Brexit Withdrawal Agreement. Here's how they can get permanent residency according to an immigration expert.

item.title: PODCAST: Why fewer foreigners are becoming French and how to fix France's second home quandary?
item.description: Welcome back to Talking France - this week's podcast covers a new scheme on a French island offering thousands of euros for second home owners, plus we look at why the French burn down speed cameras and how to sound like a local using animals.

item.title: Which nationalities get the most EU Blue Cards and where do they go?
item.description: The EU hands out thousands of Blue Cards to highly-skilled third country nationals each year, according to the latest figures. But which nationalities receive the most and which EU country gives out the most?

item.title: The ski destinations you can reach by train from Germany
item.description: One of the advantages of living in Europe is having access to a great transcontinental train network. In the winter months you don't need a car to get from Germany to these stunning winter sport destinations in the Alps.

item.title: Why is Musk so opposed to Spain banning social media for under-16s?
item.description: The world's richest man has called Pedro Sánchez a "tyrant" and a “fascist totalitarian” after Spain's prime minister announced a planned social media ban for teens. Why is the tech billionaire - and father of 14 children - so opposed to the move?
